newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia cancels proposed changes to mining laws.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia cancels proposed changes to mining laws.

text.p: Indonesia has cancelled changes it had proposed to mining regulations following negative feedback from the industry, the director-general of mining Adjat Sudradjat told Reuters on Friday.

"There will be no changes. We will now go back to the COW that had been initialled (last year)," he said after chairing a half-hour meeting with representatives from 60 companies which had applied for the seventh-generation contracts of work (COW) for mineral mining and the third-generation contracts covering the coal sector.
Adjat said industry representatives had described the proposed changes as not practical and difficult to implement.
"Almost all of them were not in favour," he said.
Adjat declined to say if the proposals would be included in the next batch of contracts to be issued by the government.
He said the seventh-generation mineral COW and the third-generation COW would soon be sent to parliament for formal approval.
The proposed changes had included requiring mining companies to allocate at least a 10-percent stake in future ventures to the government free of charge.

They also covered government proposals that mining companies with operations in Indonesia share capital gains made on stock exchanges outside the country with their shareholders and that the raising of additional capital through a public offering of shares would have to be done in Indonesia.
Some mining analysts said the capital gains proposal would be virtually impossible to enforce, while Indonesia did not have the capital to finance large-scale exploration work.
Coal mining companies were, among others, required to divest 51 percent of their equity in future projects to Indonesians by the 10th year of operations.
